decisions.reason: The Banach-space local-minimum hypothesis was standard and the line argument valid, but def-local-extremum only defines real-domain minima. Added the exact norm-ball definition in Statement and grounded F1 in it; the real-domain citation now applies only to the reduced scalar function. Zero directions, two-sided admissibility, Fermat, order-one Taylor and continuity of the second derivative establish the unchanged conclusion without a new choice premise.

F2 incorrectly described countable infima as real-valued closure: inf_k(-k)=-infinity. The supplier proves extended-real measurability, which is sufficient here. Corrected F2 and explicitly made g=liminf g_k extended-real; outside the common null set it equals the finite composition, and completeness makes each real Borel preimage measurable after arbitrary null-set values.

All four trace interfaces and the fractional boundary-space definition require n>=2, while Statement and Given omitted it. Added this explicit hypothesis, matching the existing contract's intended boundary-space range rather than abandoning a defined one-dimensional trace claim. Under AC, bounded linear T and ker T=W0 give nonemptiness, the affine identity, convexity, norm closedness, and weak closedness.

The unrestricted necessity assertion is false: on K={u>=0} the functional integral u has a minimum at 0 but directional derivative along 1 equals |Omega|. Qualified necessity to Gateaux differentiability with an interior open-set minimum or two-sided affine variations, and to the integral theorem's fixed-trace hypotheses. Added the one-sided constrained caveat and stated the exact convex variational-inequality converse; polynomial counterexamples remain valid.

F1 attributed the equation to a trace-based theorem valid only for n>=2. The existing exact quadratic expansion proves the bounded first variation for every n>=1, so the example itself is valid. Grounded stationarity in that computation and made the theorem comparison conditional on n>=2 and p=2 growth. Testing with u and Poincare gives the unique stationary point 0; a nonzero bump and arbitrarily small scalar multiples disprove local minimality, while large multiples make J unbounded below.

The oscillatory H1 sequence and energy comparison correctly prove failure of weak sequential lower semicontinuity, but F5 and the conclusion overclaimed necessity of convexity for the cited existence theorem. The example is one-dimensional, violates its quadratic upper-growth condition, and already has minimisers u_k with value 0. Replaced that overclaim with these exact caveats and an explicit functional nonconvexity check using u1 and -u1; preserved the sawtooth, weak-convergence proof and extended-value convention.
